name: Buffer Under-read
principle: The product reads a buffer through an index or pointer that can point before the buffer start. This can disclose adjacent memory, leak addresses for ASLR bypass, or crash on invalid memory.
detection_signals: signed index used in array[index] after only index < len check
array[index] read in error/logging path after index failed validation
buf[offset] or *(buf + offset) where offset is signed and no offset >= 0 check
p--, --p, or p -= n followed by *p without p >= base or p > base guard
reverse scan loop such as while (*--p != c) without p > base condition
memcpy/memcmp/strncmp/read using src + offset where offset can be negative
negative_signals: read guarded by index >= 0 && index < len in the same control path
pointer read guarded by p >= base && p < base + len before dereference
reverse scan loop checks p > base before decrement-and-dereference
signed index is validated nonnegative before cast to size_t
C++ std::vector::at or std::span::at used and exception is handled
false_defense_traps: checking only index < len misses negative indexes
checking only p < end misses pointers before base
casting negative signed index to size_t before validation creates a huge positive value
validating normal path but reading array[index] in the error message
treating all out-of-bounds reads as upper-bound over-reads and missing under-read direction
verification_focus: Can any read address or index evaluate to a location before the target buffer start?

consequence_chains.trigger: minimum index is not checked before array[index]
consequence_chains.consequence: negative index reads memory before the buffer

consequence_chains.trigger: integer underflow makes an offset or index negative
consequence_chains.consequence: read pointer moves before the buffer and may leak memory or crash

patch_principle: Validate both lower and upper bounds before every buffer read.
Reject negative indexes and offsets before pointer arithmetic or size_t casts.
Guard backward scans with a base-address termination condition.
Avoid reading invalid indexes in diagnostics or error paths.
Use bounds-checked containers or APIs where practical.
